_comment: Task 2 additional training negatives: real, cluttered, in-the-wild people, with no screen, whiteboard, document or slide text. Fixes the person covariate shift, where probe FP was about 51%.
_label: category=negative_clean, which prepare_dataset maps to label 0 (do not record). Each new slug becomes a subclass under negative_clean and enters the training pool automatically.
_design: Deliberately different from the existing people_portrait, which is clean studio portraiture, and deliberately weighted toward non-office, non-meeting everyday scenes (street, market, commute, home, sport, service work, outdoor activity). Three reasons: maximise diversity of scene, lighting and composition; keep the probe a genuine held-out generalisation test rather than a mirror of the training negatives; and reduce the chance of pulling in images that contain a readable screen.
_distinct_from_probe: The query wording is deliberately different from the subclasses of probe_person_noscreen. Zero overlap at the image level is guaranteed by the downloader's global Pexels-ID dedup plus scripts/guard_probe_overlap.py afterwards, which checks by ID and by perceptual hash. Scene types may still overlap with the probe.
_manual_qc: After downloading, manually remove any image containing readable screen, whiteboard, document, slide or code-screen text, otherwise positives end up in the negative class. Removal goes through the guard script's quarantine, which moves rather than deletes, so it stays traceable.
